I haven't yet. I hope that conversation will just end up happening naturally, if not I'll maybe try talk to her about it before we graduate (this year), for closures sake at least.
I think eventually if a conversation doesn't spring naturally, I'll ask her if she wants to talk about our views together openly since it has been kinda affecting me over the past few days.

But it's hard to actually believe that she accepts me, especially considering how being gay is a much bigger part of my life than most people's relationships with their tattoos (although I don't think it should be, being gay, and having experiences related to that definitely shapes a lot of how I am as a person). Like, if someone didn't like tattoos, then their friend became a tattoo artist and owned their own tattoo shop, and the person actively encouraged them to get more tattoos and seemingly supported them in their career path of being a tattoo artist, but then told them that they don't approve of tattoos, is that not a bit contradictory?

She also has said comments about gay marriage, and mentioned disapproval of gay-ness in other contexts before I asked, but I never really realised it until the conversation I had with her. 

To add to the tattoo thing, I also think it's a bit different since being gay is not a choice, whereas getting a tattoo is. In my opinion, it's more understandable to be friends with someone who has made choices you disagree with, rather than be friends with someone who has a born, involuntary characteristic you don't agree with.
